title: Plantaardige olien - perskoeken en schroot
commodity_branch: Plantaardig - akkerbouw > Oliehoudende gewassen (ook Varia > Olien, vetten)
why_it_is_a_gap: Largest unresolved block in the register: 20% of MONBIO 4.0's residual total, zero L4 rows beneath it. Also a DOUBLE PLACEMENT - the identical 1.149.000 t is filed as C-335 under Plantaardig-akkerbouw and as C-280 under Varia; same for 1.376.000 t (C-524/C-465) in MONBIO 3.0.
proposed_fix: Split into named oilseed meals at L4 (koolzaadschroot, sojaschroot, zonnebloemschroot, lijnzaadschroot, maiskiemschroot) - the source already reports matching crude-oil production per oilseed (C-324..C-328). Separately decide which parent the schroot figure belongs to and retire the duplicate.
NOTES: Agrees C-342/C-532 are selectable waste. NOT convinced the split into fractions can rest on production volume alone: unsure these oilseeds are the only source of the waste in C-342/C-532, and whether each contributes proportionally. DOUBLE PLACEMENT: keep C-335 (drop C-280).

title: Vleesverwerking - 631.000 t behind one poultry row
why_it_is_a_gap: Only 13,3% resolves, and the one row that does (poultry offal C-299) is selectable only because Prodcom gives poultry its own code. C-297 and C-295 NAME species (runderen, varkens, schapen, geiten) and are aggregates only because the nomenclature lists them together; C-298 and C-308 are genuine category totals.
proposed_fix: Split the species-named rows into L4 streams per animal (rund, varken, schaap/geit), matching how Gevogelte already sits. Leave C-298 and C-308 as aggregates.
NOTES: Split C-277 into edible vs non-edible, then per animal within each. Notes C-308+C-298 does not equal C-277, and questions how to link production to a waste ratio. C-297 is animal FAT and can be an L4. [Checked: C-308+C-298=386.723 vs C-277 631.000 - expected, C-277 is a NACE sector total and the others are Prodcom product rows that do not tile it. C-308 DOES reconcile: C-295+C-299+C-296 = 216.610 vs 217.672, 0,5% rounding - C-296 was the missing term. C-297 confirmed as 'Rund-, schapen-, geiten- of varkensvet (Prodcom 101150)'.]

title: Zuivel - every waste row at L3, every L4 slot taken by production
why_it_is_a_gap: This is why milk never appears in the selection. Every dairy row carrying an L4 is a hoofdstroom (Koemelk 4.396.737, Kaas, Boter); every dairy WASTE row sits at L3 with L4 blank. Mass is the same order as poultry offal, which IS selected. Root cause is in the dictionary: Melk is an L3 whose L4 members are species, but no source reports dairy waste by species, so the L4 slot is permanently empty on the residual side.
proposed_fix: Add an L4 member 'Melk' (unsplit) under L3 Melk for sources that do not split by species, and re-level the five waste rows onto it. Values and names unchanged.
NOTES: All agri-food waste here should be selectable. Accepts that melk/zuivel waste is itself a kind of aggregate (different milks, different cheeses, yoghurt) but holds that zuivelwaste and milkwaste are legitimate selectable stream items.

title: Maalderij - zemelen en gries
why_it_is_a_gap: 361.068 t in MONBIO 4.0 - larger than every horticultural stream in the selection except bloemkoolloof. Aggregates only because the Prodcom labels bundle a named stream with a leftover ('Zemelen, slijpsel EN ANDERE RESTEN'; 'Gries, griesmeel en pellets van granen, N.E.G.').
proposed_fix: Promote 'Zemelen' to an L4 stream under Granen, accepting a small 'andere resten' tail in the printed figure. JUDGEMENT NEEDED on Gries: the n.e.g. marker is a genuine residual signal, so it may have to stay an aggregate.
NOTES: These are L3 aggregates but should be selectable like milk. Place at L4: even though they are a combination of items, those items arise naturally as a combination and cannot be split. Applies to BOTH zemelen and gries - overrides the proposed caution on the n.e.g. marker.

title: Bostel (brewers' spent grain)

why_it_is_a_gap: BSG is captured at 134.653 t but cannot be selected - the Prodcom label bundles bostel with 'afvallen van branderijen', which trips the residual-class rule. One of the best-characterised side streams in the field, with a Flemish beer production figure available to size it against.
proposed_fix: Promote 'Bostel' to an L4 stream. PLACEMENT DECISION: under Granen (the crop ladder), or under Varia > Dranken per the v2.5 rule that a processing product goes under its sector.

title: Bietenpulp selectable in one edition, an aggregate in the other
claim_ids: C-382 (L5, selectable); C-575 (L5, selectable); C-555 (L3, aggregate)
why_it_is_a_gap: Same material treated two ways. MONBIO 4.0 has C-382 as a clean L5 fraction under Suikerbiet, IN the selection. MONBIO 3.0 has C-575 at L5 (337.649 t) AND C-555 at L3 as a 661.550 t aggregate under a different parent (Varia > Suiker), bundling beet pulp with cane and other sugar-industry residues. The two editions are not comparable on a stream the selection actually uses.
proposed_fix: Decide whether C-555 is the PARENT of C-575 (then record it in aggregate_coverage.csv with the right coverage) or a rival measurement on a wider scope. Either way put both under one parent so the editions line up.
NOTES: Reads C-555 as the parent of C-575, and wants the DIFFERENCE to become a new selectable L4 'uitgeperst suikerriet'. *** BLOCKED - NEEDS REVIEWER SIGN-OFF: (1) 661.550-337.649=323.901 is not printed by the source, so creating it is a derivation the protocol forbids; (2) the residue is cane PLUS 'andere afvallen van de suikerindustrie', not cane alone; (3) the two rows use different bases - C-555 is a 69% export-proxy Flemish share, C-575 is grondgebiedbasis - so they are two accountings, not parent and child, and the subtraction is not sound. ***

NOTES: Dode dieren (C-267/C-448) NOT needed - drop. Slachthuisreststromen, huiden en botten (C-102) becomes an L4 under Vlees.
